_comment: Eastern Cape Department of Education Grade 11 Mathematical Literacy P2, November 2025 provincial common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers extracted from the text layer of the official PDFs
(paper2.pdf, paper2_memo.pdf) and read against the rendered pages. Mathematical
Literacy questions hang off shared scenario boxes: the scenario (tables, graphs, plans and maps
described in bracketed words) is the 'context' of the first sub-question of each block and applies
to the sub-questions after it. memo_answer gives the guideline's working and final answer with
decimal commas kept; the guideline's mark codes (M method, A accuracy, CA consistent accuracy, RT
reading from table, C conclusion, O opinion, S simplification, R rounding) and level tags are left out.
FORMAT: 100 marks, 2 hours, four compulsory questions (Q1 24, Q2 27, Q3 23, Q4 26). ANNEXURE A (map
of Pilgrim's Rest), ANNEXURE B (map of Mpumalanga) and ANNEXURE C (table and tablecloth diagrams) are
in the separate addendum, tracked as paper2_addendum.pdf; map-read answers come from the guideline.

questions.context: QUESTION 1 | 1.1 Andrea bakes wedding cakes. The most popular cake she bakes is a carrot cake with cream cheese frosting. Study the recipe below and answer the questions that follow. INGREDIENTS: 350 g self-raising flour; 325 g dark soft brown sugar; 1½ teaspoons fine sea salt; 2 teaspoons cinnamon; 200 ml olive oil; 1 teaspoon vanilla extract; 4 large eggs; 250 g grated peeled carrots; 75 g chopped pecan nuts; 4 tablespoons milk. FOR CREAMY FROSTING: 10 ounces cream cheese; 1¼ cups (140 g) powdered sugar; ¾ cup (80 ml) cold heavy cream; ½ cup salted butter. METHOD: 1. Preheat the oven to 356 °F. 2. Grease and line the bottom and sides of two round cake pans with a double layer of greaseproof paper. 3. Mix the flour, salt, sugar, cinnamon, chopped pecan nuts and grated carrots in a large bowl. 4. Beat together the eggs, olive oil, vanilla extract and milk in a large jug and add to the flour mixture. Mix well. 5. Divide the cake batter between the prepared cake pans. Bake for 35-45 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. 6. Cool the cake layers in the pans for 15 minutes, then carefully turn the cake layers out onto cooling racks. CREAM CHEESE FROSTING: 1. Once the cake layers are completely cooled off, mix the cream cheese and butter in a blender for 1 and a half minutes. 2. Add powdered sugar until frosting is creamy. Whip cold heavy cream into the mixture for 3 minutes until light and fluffy. 3. Cover the cake in frosting - this will take up to 15 minutes. BAKING CONVERSIONS: 1 cup = 250 ml; 1 tablespoon = 15 ml; 1 teaspoon = 5 ml. [Adapted from https://www.inspiredtaste.net]
questions.text: Calculate the time (in minutes) to cover the cake with the cream cheese frosting.
questions.topic: Measurement: conversions, time and estimating
questions.memo_answer: Total time = 1,5 minutes + 3 minutes + 15 minutes = 19,5 minutes

questions.text: Siphokazi claims that if she travels at an average speed of 80 km/h and leaves her home at 12:45, she will arrive in Standerton at 16:05, without any stops. Verify, with the necessary calculations, whether her claim is VALID. You may use the following formula: Speed = Distance ÷ Time
questions.topic: Maps: scales, street maps and directions
questions.memo_answer:
Time = 276 km ÷ 80 km/h = 3,45 hours
0,45 x 60 = 27 minutes; travel time = 3 h 27 min
Arrival time = 12:45 + 03:27 = 16:12
Siphokazi's claim is not valid.

questions.context: QUESTION 3 | 3.1 Wilmien decided to sell imported coffee beans in resealable containers to generate funds in aid of a wheelchair for her physically disabled brother. The diagram below shows two types of containers that Wilmien can choose from. The containers will be covered in petroleum-based plastic. [RECTANGULAR-SHAPED CONTAINER: length 150 mm, width 0,08 m, height 14,5 cm. CYLINDRICAL-SHAPED CONTAINER: radius 50 mm (marked across the top from the centre), height 12 cm.] The following formulae may be used: Volume of a cylinder = π x radius² x height, where π = 3,142; Volume of a rectangular prism = length x width x height; Total surface area of a rectangular prism = 2(l x w) + 2(l x h) + 2(w x h).
questions.text: Determine the volume of the cylindrical-shaped container in cubic centimetres (cm3).
questions.topic: Measurement: perimeter, area, volume and material costs
questions.memo_answer:
Radius = 50 ÷ 10 = 5 cm
Volume = 3,142 x 5² x 12 = 942,6 cm³

questions.text: Determine the total surface of the rectangular-shaped container that needs to be covered in petroleum-based plastic. Give your answer rounded to the nearest thousand square millimetres (mm2).
questions.topic: Measurement: perimeter, area, volume and material costs

questions.text: The petroleum-based plastic that Wilmien will use to cover the containers is sold at R27,55/m2. Calculate the cost to cover 50 of the rectangular-shaped containers with this plastic. NOTE: The petroleum-based plastic can only be bought in whole square metres (m2).
questions.topic: Measurement: perimeter, area, volume and material costs
questions.memo_answer:
Amount of plastic needed = 91 000 ÷ 1 000 000 = 0,091 m² x 50 = 4,55 m² ≈ 5 m²
Cost of plastic = 5 m² x R27,55 = R137,75

questions.text: Wilmien realised that she cannot fill the containers to maximum capacity. Instead, she fills the containers with coffee beans to a height that is 7% less than the container height. Show that the height of the coffee beans in the cylindrical container is 11,2 cm.
questions.topic: Measurement: perimeter, area, volume and material costs

questions.text: A sales representative advised Wilmien that the volume of the most economical container should not exceed 1 200 cm3. Wilmien thus claim that the rectangular- shaped container would be the most economical. Verify, with the necessary calculations, whether Wilmien’s claim is VALID.
questions.topic: Measurement: perimeter, area, volume and material costs
questions.memo_answer:
Volume of cylindrical container = 942,6 cm³
Rectangular container: 15 cm x 8 cm x 14,5 cm = 1 740 cm³
Her statement is not valid.

questions.text: Provide ONE reason why Wilmien would want to wrap the containers in petroleum-based plastic.
questions.topic: Plans: assembly instructions and packaging
questions.memo_answer: To keep the coffee beans fresh OR to protect the container against breakage (accept any other relevant explanation)

[Layout plan with numbered stores 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 11, 12 and 13 (there is no store 8 or 10) and unnumbered outlets The Pizza Den, Sports, Kohl's, Food & More, Pet Shop, McFlurries and Bellis Fair Cinema; key: public restroom, ATM, mall entrance.]
questions.text: Determine the probability, as a percentage, that Wilmien will be selling her coffee beans to a store with an uneven number.
questions.topic: Probability: simple and compound events

questions.text: Wilmien arrived at the mall to do her deliveries at 08:30 and she concluded her delivery at 10:15. Wilmien claimed that she walked at an average speed of 1,4 miles per hour and thus covered a travelling distance inside the mall of more than 4 km. Verify, with the necessary calculations, whether Wilmien’s claim is VALID. NOTE: 1 mile = 1,60934 km You may use the following formula: Distance = Speed × Time
questions.topic: Measurement: conversions, time and estimating
questions.memo_answer:
Travelling time = 10:15 - 08:30 = 01:45; 45 ÷ 60 = 0,75 h; time = 1,75 hours
Distance = 1,4 miles/h x 1,75 h = 2,45 miles x 1,60934 = 3,942883 km
Her statement is invalid.
OR speed = 1,4 x 1,60934 = 2,253076 km/h; distance = 2,253076 x 1,75 = 3,942883 km; invalid

questions.context: 4.2 The Pizza Den is a new establishment inside the shopping mall that makes delicious pizzas. A picture of the sliced pizza and its packaging box is shown in the diagram below. The pizza has a diameter of 42 cm. [Diagram: the round pizza centred in a square box; dimensions of box are 45 cm x 45 cm; the gap D between the pizza and the box is marked on each side.]
questions.text: Determine the area of the pizza box, rounded to the nearest ten square centimetres (cm2). You may use the following formula: Area of a square = side × side
questions.topic: Measurement: perimeter, area, volume and material costs
questions.memo_answer: Area = 45 cm x 45 cm = 2 025 cm² ≈ 2 030 cm²

questions.text: Determine the value of D.
questions.topic: Measurement: perimeter, area, volume and material costs
questions.memo_answer:
2D = 45 cm - 42 cm = 3 cm
D = 3 cm ÷ 2 = 1,5 cm

questions.text: Calculate the area of one slice of the pizza if it is cut in eight equal slices as illustrated in the picture above. You may use the following formula: Area of a circle = π × radius2, where π = 3,142
questions.topic: Measurement: perimeter, area, volume and material costs
questions.memo_answer:
Area of pizza = 3,142 x 21² = 1 385,622 cm²
Area of one slice = 1 385,622 ÷ 8 = 173,20 cm²

questions.context: 4.3 The table used inside The Pizza Den where customers can enjoy their food is shown in ANNEXURE C. The tables are covered with PVC tablecloths with an overhang of 35 cm around the table. [ANNEXURE C: round table top with diameter 160 cm and thickness 0,7 cm on a support pole with a base of height 2,8 cm; the tablecloth hangs 35 cm over the edge.]
questions.text: Calculate the radius of the plastic PVC tablecloth that is used to cover the tables.
questions.topic: Measurement: perimeter, area, volume and material costs
questions.memo_answer:
Diameter = 160 cm + 35 cm + 35 cm = 230 cm
Radius = 230 ÷ 2 = 115 cm

questions.text: Calculate the height of the support pole (in cm) if the total height of the table is 78 cm.
questions.topic: Measurement: perimeter, area, volume and material costs
questions.memo_answer: Height of support pole = 78 cm - (2,8 cm + 0,7 cm) = 74,5 cm
